reviews.title: Constant freezing
reviews.text: Have used the app for about a year and a half. Really helpful and appreciate the pronunciation but the constant freezing is EXTREMELY aggravating

reviews.title: Freezes
reviews.text: Fed up of this app crashing!! Hasn't been updated in 2 years and not sure anyone's monitoring these reviews. Awful

reviews.title: Why require location for a dictionary app?
reviews.text: The app requires that the user permits location data prior to usage for so called “network access”. This doesn’t pass the smell test and appears gratuitous. The privacy policy states that it retain the full IP address for 14 days. This also seems way more than expected for a reference app.

reviews.title: Security Risk
reviews.text: Already had to give it a one-star simply due to the security risk this app poses. I shouldn't need to give an app local network permissions just to access a dictionary. This is really invasive and they don't provide any explanation for why they require this, which is really shady. So I'll be looking elsewhere, but I would advise against  using this app if you value your privacy.

reviews.title: Nice interface, terrible performance
reviews.text: Love the interface and examples, but it’s extremely slow and keeps hanging. Have to keep restarting it and it always takes 3-5 seconds to activate the keyboard each time I come back to it.

reviews.title: shouldn’t require local network access to work
reviews.text: why does the app require local network access??

reviews.title: Great app, bricks itself without local network access
reviews.text:
The translation functionality, also available on the website, is fantastic, showing lots of example uses in context, lots of samples of translations from a wide variety of source document pairs.
The app insists on, not Internet access, which is available to (nearly/every) app, but being able to scan the local network to allow any use of the app.

Great core products, weird insistence on permissions at doesn’t need, that are not relevant for most users. I have a hard time imagining who they are relevant for, some kind of corporate deployment where you run a linguee server.
